claims.text: Adding a Ti or Cr intermediate adhesion layer before DLC deposition will improve bonding between the DLC coating and Ti-6Al-4V.
The adhesion-layer/DLC treatment will approximately double the near-surface hardness of Ti-6Al-4V.
The adhesion-layer/DLC treatment will reduce Ti-6Al-4V wear volume by more than 50% under aggressive sliding conditions.
A 1–2 µm DLC coating can be deposited on the pretreated and interlayer-coated alloy using plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition below 250°C with controlled CH4 and hydrogen mixtures.
The proposed processing will produce a high-density amorphous DLC coating with substantial sp³ bonding.
The engineered adhesion layer will firmly bond the DLC coating to Ti-6Al-4V.
The adhesion layer provides robust DLC–substrate bonding.
The DLC layer is superhard and has low friction.
The DLC barrier will minimize surface abrasion during mechanical loading.
The DLC barrier will minimize surface plastic deformation during mechanical loading.
Reduced abrasion and plastic deformation will increase surface hardness and wear resistance.
The predicted hardness and wear improvements will hold during room-temperature sliding wear tests.
The tribological performance of DLC coatings is well documented.
The magnitude of the hardness and wear improvements depends on successful adhesion enhancement and long-term interface durability under cyclic stress.
